summary: This work presents the first distance-preserving unitary encoding scheme for preparing Pauli eigenstates $|0\rangle_L$ and $|+\rangle_L$ in surface codes, generalizing strategies discovered by reinforcement learning for the surface-17 code to arbitrary distances and both rotated and unrotated variants. The scheme uses only geometrically local gates with circuit depth $\mathcal{O}(d)$, avoiding classical feedback while preserving the code's fault distance during state preparation.
motivation: Standard unitary encodings for surface codes suffer from constant fault-distance regardless of code distance $d$, while measurement-based schemes require slow measurements that dominate overall protocol time, particularly problematic on neutral atoms and trapped-ion platforms where measurements are 50–100× slower than gates.
method: The authors design stabilizer-expanding circuits that grow Pauli logical states row-by-row using geometrically local two-qubit gates, with two variants: one using ancilla qubits as bridges between data qubits (compatible with superconducting architectures), and one assuming full intra-plaquette connectivity (suitable for neutral atoms and trapped ions). Gate ordering is carefully scheduled to keep hook errors correctable, preserving fault distance for the corresponding error type.
result: Numerical simulations under depolarizing noise show the ancilla-free variant reduces logical error rates by up to an order of magnitude compared to measurement-based encoding for $d=3$ to $11$, despite identical circuit depth; the ancilla variant underperforms measurement-based encoding due to additional error sources, but unitary encoding eliminates measurement overhead that dominates protocol duration on platforms with slow measurements.
